data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"RFC 9110 defines safe and idempotent as orthogonal in principle, with overlap only because the empty set of side effects happens to be idempotent. The append-only log requires idempotence precisely, and the safe property is a red herring: safety forbids the very operation (state mutation) the log exists to perform. The precise distinction is that safety constrains the effect itself (must be null), while idempotence constrains the effect under repetition (must be constant). The log needs constant-on-repetition, not null-effect.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If RFC 9110's definitions are not set-theoretic in this way and the formalization is an imposed overlay, it may not match the standard's actual language.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If one can construct an append-only log where repeated appends produce different but replay-deterministic states (e.g., timestamps preserved), the 'constant effect' requirement may be too strong.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Safety: the set of state transitions caused by f is empty. Idempotence: the set of state transitions caused by f\u2218f equals the set caused by f. For an append-only log, f's transition set is non-empty (it adds an event), so safety is violated. But f\u2218f's transition set can equal f's if the second invocation is a dedup no-op\u2014achieving idempotence. The log requires this: constant-on-repetition, explicitly not null-effect.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
